## Highlights

Adds official JavaScript and TypeScript bindings for Zova, distributed on npm
as `zova-js` with prebuilt Node-API packages for every supported platform.

## What's changed

- Added synchronous JavaScript APIs for database lifecycle, SQL statements,
  transactions, objects, vectors, public graph operations, and bundled
  extension lifecycle.
- Added a separate queued `AsyncDatabase` API that runs native work through the
  Node worker pool while preserving per-database FIFO ordering and explicit
  close behavior.
- Added TypeScript declarations, runnable SQL/object/vector/graph examples, and
  blocking Node ESM, Node CommonJS, and Bun runtime coverage.
- Added prebuilt native npm packages for macOS arm64/x86_64, glibc Linux
  arm64/x86_64, and Windows x86_64.
- Added release-artifact assembly, clean-package installation smoke tests, and
  protected npm publication for `zova-js` and its native companion packages.
- Added support for an initial granular npm publishing token and token-free
  trusted publishing through GitHub Actions OIDC for later releases.

## Compatibility

- The npm package name is `zova-js`; the Zova product name, `.zova` file
  extension, native library name, Rust crate, Python package, and Go module
  remain unchanged.
- Package and C ABI versions advance to `0.26.0`. The `.zova` on-disk format
  remains format 9; no database migration is required from Zova 0.25.0.
- Node.js 22 and 24 and Bun are supported. Electron, Deno, browsers, musl
  Linux, Windows arm64, and WASM are not claimed in this release.
- Advanced opaque-key graph scans, edge payload APIs, and fresh-build sessions
  remain C ABI and raw `zova-sys` capabilities and are not exposed by the
  high-level JavaScript package.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/ata-sesli/zova/compare/v0.25.0...v0.26.0
